findings.title: RSS feed content is stored and rendered as unsanitized raw HTML (stored XSS)
findings.body: poll_feed passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The new `Post#cook` returns the raw string unchanged for such posts, so `post.cooked` contains the feed HTML completely unfiltered — including any `<script>` or event-handler attributes (unescapeHTML even turns `<script>` back into a live tag). That cooked HTML is rendered unsanitized on the forum and in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. A single malicious or compromised feed entry would therefore execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browsers of all forum visitors and staff. The feed URL being admin-configured does not make every item in a third-party feed trustworthy; the content should be run through a sanitizer/whitelist before import.

findings.title: i.content can be nil, crashing the hourly feed job
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `.scrub` on `i.content`, but SimpleRSS only populates `content` when the feed item has a content:encoded element. Plain RSS 2.0 items typically only have a `description`, and Atom items use `summary`/`content` differently, so for many real feeds `i.content` will be nil and the job will raise NoMethodError. Since the job declares `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the entire hourly poll silently fails and no topics are imported. The code should fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` or guard against nil.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: The absolutize logic checks `href.start_with?('/')` and prepends the site's scheme+host, which also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Such a URL gets rewritten to `http://sourcehost.com/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`, producing a broken link/image. Protocol-relative URLs are common in feed content (especially for images/CDNs), so imported topics will contain dead links. The check should skip values starting with `//`.

findings.title: postMessage origin validation uses substring match instead of equality
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any message whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl, rather than comparing origins exactly. This is a fragile trust check for a cross-origin message handler; it should compare the event origin against the forum's origin (e.g. `e.origin !== discourseOrigin`) so that only the actual Discourse iframe can drive the resize behavior, and so the check doesn't silently misbehave when discourseUrl has unexpected forms (paths, ports, trailing slashes).

findings.title: Retroactively editing an existing migration to add force: true
findings.body: The PR modifies the already-released migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. Migrations that have already run in production should not be edited — environments at different migration states will now have drifted from the checked-in definition, and `force: true` silently drops and recreates the table if the migration is ever re-run (e.g. after a rollback or in a partially-migrated environment), destroying any data in top_topics. New behavior belongs in a new migration.
